duration.from: Ordinance No. 26-20 proposes a temporary two-year moratorium; introduced on the consent agenda at the September 10, 2026 regular council meeting, which set a public hearing and action vote for October 8, 2026. No adoption vote had occurred as of 2026-09-23. A separate, differently-worded ordinance to block data center construction failed 4-2 at the August 13, 2026 council meeting; Ordinance 26-20 is a distinct, later measure.

current_status.from: Pending as of 2026-09-23. Ordinance 26-20, establishing a temporary two-year moratorium on the acceptance, processing, approval, or issuance of permits as well as construction, establishment, and operation of data centers within Houston city limits, was introduced on the council's September 10, 2026 consent agenda; a public hearing and council action vote are scheduled for October 8, 2026. The introduction followed an August 13, 2026 meeting at which a differently drafted anti-data-center ordinance failed 4-2, and coincides with council opposition to a proposed ~20,000-acre state land transfer to AIDEA (Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority) near Houston that could host data centers.
current_status.to: Adopted unanimously on 2026-10-08 and signed by the mayor. Section 6 makes the ordinance effective upon passage and signature for two years from that effective date, subject to earlier repeal or extension. The signature is undated; exact effective and expiration dates and any subsequent action remain unverified.
